name: Hatat
title: Descendant of Judah
summary: Hatat is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles as a descendant of Judah through Othniel. He is known only from the genealogies in the Books of Chronicles and has no further narrative role in the Bible. His significance lies in being part of the tribe of Judah's genealogy.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Judah's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Hatat is mentioned as a son of Othniel in the genealogy of Judah's descendants in 1 Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Part of Kenaz's Lineage
keyEvents.description: Hatat belongs to the lineage of Kenaz, which is an important branch of the tribe of Judah, and is thus connected to Othniel's work as a judge in Israel.

keyEvents.title: Othniel's Descendants Recorded
keyEvents.description: In the extensive genealogical overview in the Books of Chronicles, Othniel's sons are recorded, including Hatat, as part of Israel's tribal history after the return from exile.

keyEvents.title: Connection to the Tribe of Judah
keyEvents.description: Hatat is part of the broader listing of the clans of the tribe of Judah, which begins in 1 Chronicles chapter 4 and highlights the tribe's significance in Israel's history.
